title: Sulfur Metabolism and Pathogenesis in Fungi and Organisms
summary: This cluster revolves around the role of sulfur in various biological processes, particularly in fungi and organisms. Sulfur metabolism is involved in the production of sulfur amino acid biosynthetic pathway, which is a pathogen of Aspergillus fumigatus and Cryptococcus neoformans. Candida albicans has several genes and proteins related to sulfur metabolism, including Met30 and Met31, and utilizes methionine synthase. Glutathione is involved in the utilization of sulfur, and sulfur is vital to the metabolism of organisms. Additionally, sulfur metabolism is linked to the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis and the production of methionine synthase.
